. An attributed string brings its own attributes, and drawing follows those: with no
in the string, the text has no truncation behavior to apply and clips.

The same rows had a second defect with the same shape. The tick lived in a 24pt table column and the label in the next column, each returned bare as its own cell view. Neither carried a vertical constraint, so a 14pt checkbox and an 11pt label each sat wherever their own sizing put them in a 17pt row, a point or two apart.
Long paths clip mid-word. No ellipsis appears, in either truncation direction.
The tick box and its label are visibly off each other's centre line down the list.
No constraint or console warning: nothing is unsatisfiable, the attribute is simply absent.
Put the truncation in the string, not on the field:
Every run of the string needs the attribute — a run appended without it keeps the default behavior for its own range.
For the alignment, one cell view owns both controls and centres them (

as conveniences that build a paragraph style for the plain string it draws. Hand it an attributed string and those conveniences are bypassed: the string's own attributes are what
reads. The field looks correctly configured in code and in the debugger, which is why this reads as a layout problem rather than a missing attribute.
Two self-sizing views in two columns have nothing tying them together vertically. A row is one cell view with constraints, or it is two controls that happen to look aligned at one font size.
whenever a cell shows an attributed string. Truncation, alignment, and line spacing set on the field are dead code there — delete them rather than leaving them as a claim the code does not honor.
Never split a row's controls across table columns to line them up. One
constraints per control is the unit that stays aligned across fonts, row size styles, and accessibility text sizes.

Clipping with no ellipsis is the tell for this bug. Text that truncates with an ellipsis at the wrong end is a paragraph-style value; text that just stops is a paragraph style that is not there at all.
